BeforeCardPlayed.rationale: All four C# guards are reproduced except the multiplayer owner test: MusicBox.cs:53 `CardBeingPlayed != null` -> `self._card_being_played is None`; :61 `WasUsedThisTurn` -> `not self.used_this_turn`; :65 `Type != CardType.Attack` -> `card.card_type == CardType.ATTACK`; :57 `cardPlay.Card.Owner != base.Owner` is structurally satisfied in a one-player sim. The latch assignment (MusicBox.cs:69 vs music_box.py:38) is the same.

AfterCardPlayed.issue: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4. The identity test (`cardPlay.Card == CardBeingPlayed`, MusicBox.cs:75), the Ethereal keyword, the destination pile and both state writes all match; what does not is `cardPlay.Card.CreateClone()` (MusicBox.cs:78), which the sim replaces with `make_card(card.id)` plus an upgrade replay (music_box.py:46-49) and so drops every piece of per-instance state the card carries.

BeforeSideTurnStart.rationale: C#'s BeforeSideTurnStart is audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json step 9 (before the block clear); the sim's on_player_turn_start is executed-confirmed to sit at step ~19, after the block clear and the energy reset (py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order). Only a latch RESET happens here and no card can be played between the two points -- the play phase opens at step 28 -- so both `used_this_turn` and `_card_being_played` are already cleared at every moment either codebase can observe them. Same mechanism and same verdict as relic/brilliant_scarf's and relic/beating_remnant's BeforeSideTurnStart (binding rule 3); recorded as a divergence rather than faithful because the slot genuinely differs. C#'s `participants.Contains(base.Owner.Creature)` filter (MusicBox.cs:88) is the multiplayer extra-turn guard and is structurally satisfied by a player-scoped sim hook. Rule 7: relics/brilliant_scarf.py, relics/beating_remnant.py and the turn_structure record are unhashed here.

AfterCombatEnd.maps_to: no counterpart; on_player_turn_start (music_box.py:55-57) is the only reset
AfterCombatEnd.rationale: MusicBox.cs:96-100 zeroes WasUsedThisTurn at combat end as well as at turn start; the sim keeps only the turn-start half. PROMPT.md bug class 13 requires tracing to the first READER of the stale field, and .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md's fixed Sweep A files this relic in the 'reset at TURN START, before any reader' bucket -- a SAFETY CLAIM, executed here rather than inherited. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b10.py music-box): the same relic instance run through two consecutive combats produces one Ethereal copy in BOTH, and a hand-poisoned instance carried in with `used_this_turn = True` and a stale `_card_being_played` still produces one copy in combat 2 -- because on_player_turn_start clears both fields before the play phase opens and the only readers are before_card_played and on_card_played. So the sweep's claim holds here. Contrast relic/belt_buckle, whose analogous missing reset has no turn-start shadow and is live. Rule 7: relics/belt_buckle.py and the sweeps document are unhashed here.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): CardModel.CreateClone() is a full model clone; the sim rebuilds the card from its id, so the copy loses the original's enchantment, affliction, keyword edits and cost modifiers
guards.issue: MECHANISM: MusicBox.cs:78 calls `cardPlay.Card.CreateClone()`, which is CardScope.CloneCard -> ClonePreservingMutability (CardModel.cs:2168-2179) and carries the card's upgrade level, Enchantment, Affliction, keyword edits and local energy-cost modifiers. music_box.py:46-49 builds `make_card(card.id)` and replays the upgrade levels, so ONLY the level survives. This is PROMPT.md bug class 17 and .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md Sweep E, which already lists relics/music_box.py:46 as one of its five sim sites; the mechanism is verdicted `gap` and LIVE at relic/burning_sticks G3, so one verdict per mechanism (binding rule 3) -- matched, not re-derived. EXECUTED AT THIS SITE (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b10.py music-box): a Strike carrying Tezcatara's Ember (enchantment='Tezcatara's Ember', energy_cost=0, eternal=True) is copied as enchantment=None, energy_cost=1, eternal=False -- the game hands the player a free +3-damage Ethereal Strike and the sim hands them a plain 1-cost one. A Ringing affliction is likewise dropped (original.affliction=Ringing(1) -> clone.affliction=None). REACHABILITY (both sides ported, no second relic needed for the affliction leg): Music Box is granted by the ported Vakuu event (events/vakuu.py); Tezcatara's Ember is attached to every Basic Strike by relic/nutritious_soup, audited in this same batch, from the ported Tezcatara event (events/tezcatara.py:44); and Ringing is applied to cards in hand by a ported enemy power (powers.py:1332). Music Box only ever copies an ATTACK and Nutritious Soup enchants exactly Basic Strikes, so the two intersect on the commonest card in the deck. Rule 7: CardModel.cs, relics/burning_sticks.py, enchantments.py, powers.py, events/vakuu.py, events/tezcatara.py and both sweep documents are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1: the upgrade replay loop is GUARDED (`if copy.is_upgradable`, music_box.py:48), so PROMPT.md bug class 14 does not fire here
guards.rationale: CardCmd.Upgrade skips cards whose IsUpgradable is false (CardCmd.cs:265-276; CardModel.cs:785-795) and the sim's bare Card.upgrade() (cards/base.py:146-148) has no such guard -- but this port supplies one, unlike relics/astrolabe.py:23 and relics/bone_tea.py:31 which Sweep D records as live. The loop exists only BECAUSE there is no clone helper; the one-helper fix Sweep E proposes removes it. Rule 7: CardCmd.cs, CardModel.cs, cards/base.py and the two sibling relic files are unhashed here.

guards.what: N2: per-Replay AfterCardPlayed (audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json G4) is NOT observable at this relic's site
guards.rationale: Checked deliberately because the same mechanism is a LIVE gap at three other relics in this batch (mummified_hand G3, nunchaku G1, ornamental_fan G1). Here the relic's own guards absorb it: C# fires BeforeCardPlayed and AfterCardPlayed once per play-count iteration (CardModel.cs:1929, :1959, inside the loop opened at :1904), and iteration 0's AfterCardPlayed sets `WasUsedThisTurn = true` and `CardBeingPlayed = null` (MusicBox.cs:81-82), so iteration 1's BeforeCardPlayed bails at MusicBox.cs:61 and no second copy is made. The sim fires each hook once and makes one copy. Same observable, so nothing is verdicted here -- the mechanism's verdict stays with hook_dispatch G4. Rule 7: CardModel.cs and the hook_dispatch record are unhashed here.

CardCmd.ApplyKeyword is `card.AddKeyword(keyword)` plus a visual refresh (CardCmd.cs:676-683); the sim models Ethereal as the `is_ethereal` flag on Card (cards/base.py:62), which is what the end-of-turn ethereal pass reads. Rule 7: CardCmd.cs and cards/base.py are unhashed here.

AddGeneratedCardsToCombat (CardPileCmd.cs:202-249) bails when the combat is not in progress, records a CardGenerated history entry, routes through Add(card, pile) and then fires Hook.AfterCardGeneratedForCombat. cmds.py:500-512 appends to the hand (overflowing to the discard pile at MAX_HAND_SIZE) and calls CardPileCmd._enter_combat; its own docstring names AddGeneratedCardToCombat as the mirror. The history entry is the game's save bookkeeping, which the sim's conformance layer reads rather than writes. Rule 7: CardPileCmd.cs and cmds.py are unhashed here, and the hand-overflow equivalence rests on cmds.py's docstring rather than on a line of CardPileCmd.cs that I read.

guards.what: N5: ExtraHoverTips (the Ethereal keyword tip, MusicBox.cs:23), Flash() (MusicBox.cs:77) and the AssertMutable property setters (MusicBox.cs:33, :46)
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / UpdateDisplay / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.PreviewCardPileAdd are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim. AssertMutable is the source's canonical-vs-mutable model discipline, which the sim does not model at all (one mutable object per relic); it guards against editing a canonical ModelDb entry and has no gameplay effect.
